issues.summary: No test or story guards the MigrateSafeL2Review layout fix (wrapper div removal); F2 also asks for a screenshot.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: MigrateSafeL2Review.tsx:26 is a markup-only change. A unit test that checks CSS child-selector structure would be brittle and add little. The PR already includes before/after screenshots, so F2's screenshot request is already met.

issues.summary: The isSafeMigrationCall JSDoc still describes only the unsupported-contract use case, but the function now also drives version-upgrade detection.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safe-migrations.ts:101-106 says it is "Used to avoid flagging the migration tx itself as an unsupported-contract interaction". The PR now also calls it from transaction-guards.ts:452, so the comment no longer matches its callers.

issues.summary: The new tests use object literals instead of txDataBuilder.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: transaction-guards.test.ts:190-233: the new tests copy the shape of the existing 1.3.0+ test right above them in the same describe block. txDataBuilder is used elsewhere in the file (line 338), but following the local pattern has no concrete cost.

issues.summary: No isSafeUpdateTxData test covers the zksync SafeMigration variant.
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safe-migrations.test.ts:57 already checks that isSafeMigrationCall matches the zksync variant, and isSafeUpdateTxData hands that check straight to the helper (transaction-guards.ts:452). A test at the call site would add only a little protection.

issues.summary: The new two-line comment repeats the helper's docstring.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: transaction-guards.ts:450-451 restates what the isSafeMigrationCall JSDoc says. This is purely a style preference.

issues.summary: Matching any version/variant SafeMigration address without a chain filter widens what the guard accepts.
issues.label: wrong
issues.evidence: The PR description says this widening is intentional. The guard is still gated by trustedDelegateCallTarget plus DELEGATE operation (transaction-guards.ts:446-448) and a migrate-method selector check. Official deployment addresses are deterministic across chains, so leaving out a chain filter is not a defect.

issues.summary: isSafeMigrationCall rebuilds its address list and interface selectors on every call.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: safe-migrations.ts:113-120 flatMaps over a small SAFE_VERSIONS list and creates an interface on each call. That is cheap in-memory work, and the function body is outside the PR's diff. Hoisting it would be a micro-optimisation.

issues.summary: No negative test for a migrate selector sent to a non-SafeMigration address.
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: The address check lives in isSafeMigrationCall, which safe-migrations.test.ts already covers. The existing 'arbitrary txData' test at the call site also shows that a non-migration address returns false.

issues.summary: It is unclear whether the Client Gateway marks the 1.5.0 SafeMigration as a trusted delegate-call target.
issues.label: unverifiable
issues.evidence: Whether data.trustedDelegateCallTarget is true for the 1.5.0 SafeMigration depends on how the CGW backend is configured, and this repo can't show that. The PR's screenshots suggest it works in practice.
